cards.explanation: The answer is that being allowed isn't always good for you. Paul, the apostle writing to the church in Corinth, says “but not everything is beneficial.” (1 Corinthians 6:12) Being allowed to do something and it being good for you are two different things, friends. I'm allowed to eat the whole batch of dough before it hits the oven. Doesn't mean my stomach will send me a thank you note.

The answer is True. Paul says it right there: “but I will not be mastered by anything.” (1 Corinthians 6:12) Think about your phone buzzing and you drop everything to look. That's a little thing running the show. Paul says nothing gets to be his boss, and I say amen to that.

The answer is False. Paul says food and the stomach won't last forever. He writes, “but God will destroy them both.” (1 Corinthians 6:13) Food and the stomach aren't forever things, friends. I've watched a whole tray of cookies disappear in ten minutes, and nobody was surprised.

The answer is the Lord. Paul says the body is “…for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.” (1 Corinthians 6:13) It goes both directions, friends. The body isn't a spare part sitting in a drawer, and I would know, since I spent years in a junk drawer myself. It belongs in the Lord's hands, and I can tell you hands are a good place to be.

The answer is that God will raise us also. Paul writes, “By His power God raised the Lord from the dead, and He will raise us also.” (1 Corinthians 6:14) The same power that did it for the Lord is the power behind the promise for us. That's why Paul can talk about the body as something that matters, friends. It isn't a throwaway.

The answer is False. Paul asks, “Shall I then take the members of Christ and unite them with a prostitute?” and then answers, “Never!” (1 Corinthians 6:15) He starts from the fact that their bodies are members of Christ. This is a heavy part of the letter, friends, and he doesn't water it down.

The answer is that he is one with her in body. Paul says a man who unites himself with a prostitute “is one with her in body.” (1 Corinthians 6:16) Then he backs it up with Scripture: “The two will become one flesh.” He's showing that the joining is real, friends, and he says so plainly.

The answer is spirit. Paul writes, “But he who unites himself with the Lord is one with Him in spirit.” (1 Corinthians 6:17) After all that talk about being joined in body, he turns it around. Being one with the Lord goes deep, friends, and I'm glad he said so.

The answer is that sexual sin is a sin against his own body. Paul says, “Every other sin a man can commit is outside his body, but he who sins sexually sins against his own body.” (1 Corinthians 6:18) That's why he gives the short command first: “Flee from sexual immorality.” Paul puts that command right at the front, friends.

The answer is a temple of the Holy Spirit. Paul writes, “Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you…?” (1 Corinthians 6:19) The Holy Spirit lives in them. That makes the body a special place, friends, not just the thing that gets you to work on time.

The answer is True. Paul writes about “…the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have received from God?” (1 Corinthians 6:19) They received Him from God. It's right there in the same verse as the temple, friends. That's a lot of truth packed into one verse.

The answer is to glorify God with their body. After saying “You are not your own; you were bought at a price,” Paul says, “Therefore glorify God with your body.” (1 Corinthians 6:19-20) That "Therefore" ties it all together, friends. The body is for the Lord, so Paul tells them to use it to glorify Him.
